structured_output.summary: The diff meets the acceptance criteria only for simple input with single spaces between lowercase-able words. It breaks "lowercase words joined by dashes" when the input has repeated, leading, or trailing whitespace, or other whitespace such as tabs or newlines. It also adds no tests.

issues.message: split(" ") splits on a single literal space only. Repeated spaces produce empty segments, so slugify("a  b") returns "a--b", not "a-b". Use split(/\s+/) or trim() first, e.g. s.trim().toLowerCase().split(/\s+/).join("-").
Leading or trailing spaces produce leading or trailing dashes. slugify(" hello ") returns "-hello-". Trimming before the split fixes this.
Tabs and newlines are not treated as word separators, so slugify("a\tb") returns "a\tb" with no dash. This follows from the single-space split and is covered by the same fix.
No tests accompany the new module. A small test file covering the basic case, repeated spaces, and leading/trailing whitespace would make the acceptance criteria verifiable.
